t: A **storage account** is a container for data services under one name: **blobs** (files as objects), **files** (network shares), **queues** (messages) and **tables** (simple rows). Because the name becomes part of a web address (`name.blob.core.windows.net`), it must be unique in the whole world, 3 to 24 characters, only lowercase letters and digits.

**Storage account** ek naam ke neeche data services ka dabba hai: **blobs** (files bator objects), **files** (network shares), **queues** (messages) aur **tables** (saada rows). Naam web address ka hissa banta hai (`name.blob.core.windows.net`), is liye poori duniya mein unique, 3 se 24 characters, sirf chhote harf aur hindse.
Kinds and performance
Kinds aur performance

items: **Standard general-purpose v2 (StorageV2)**: hard-disk based, all services, all redundancy options, all tiers. The default answer.
**Standard general-purpose v2 (StorageV2)**: hard-disk wala, tamam services, tamam redundancy, tamam tiers. Default jawab.
**Premium block blob**: SSD, very low latency, for block and append blobs.
**Premium block blob**: SSD, bohat kam latency, block aur append blobs ke liye.
**Premium file shares (FileStorage)**: SSD shares, SMB or NFS.
**Premium file shares (FileStorage)**: SSD shares, SMB ya NFS.

t: What you can't change afterwards: the name, the region, standard/premium, and the premium kind. What you can: redundancy, default access tier, firewall, TLS version. Old GPv1 accounts are upgraded to GPv2 in place, one way. *Infrastructure encryption* (a second layer) can be chosen only at creation.

Baad mein nahi badalta: naam, region, standard/premium, aur premium ki qism. Badal sakta hai: redundancy, default access tier, firewall, TLS version. Purane GPv1 accounts usi jagah GPv2 mein upgrade hote hain, ek tarfa. *Infrastructure encryption* (doosri teh) sirf banate waqt chuni jati hai.
Redundancy: two questions
Redundancy: do sawal

Don't memorize six names. Ask two questions. **Where are the copies in the primary region?** One datacenter (**L**RS) or three or more availability zones (**Z**RS). **Is there a copy in a second region?** Then a **G** appears: **G**RS is LRS plus geo, **GZ**RS is ZRS plus geo. Put **RA-** in front and you may *read* the second region at any time.

Che naam yaad na karein. Do sawal poochein. **Primary region mein copies kahan?** Ek datacenter (**L**RS) ya teen ya zyada availability zones (**Z**RS). **Doosre region mein copy hai?** To **G** aata hai: **G**RS yani LRS aur geo, **GZ**RS yani ZRS aur geo. Aage **RA-** lagayen to doosra region kabhi bhi *parh* sakte hain.

Data must stay in one country-region and survive a zone outage: ZRS. A read-only report app must work while the primary region is down, without failing over: RA-GRS or RA-GZRS. Test data you can recreate: LRS, the cheapest.
Data ek hi region mein rahe aur zone outage jhele: ZRS. Read-only report app primary region band hone par baghair failover chale: RA-GRS ya RA-GZRS. Dobara ban jane wala test data: LRS, sab se sasta.

Copies inside the primary region are **synchronous**: a write is confirmed after they're made. The copy to the second region is **asynchronous**, so it can be minutes behind. **Last Sync Time** tells you up to when the second region is complete. If you fail over, writes after that time may be lost.

Primary region ke andar copies **synchronous** hain: write un ke banne ke baad confirm hoti hai. Doosre region ki copy **asynchronous** hai, is liye chand minute peeche ho sakti hai. **Last Sync Time** batata hai kab tak doosra region mukammal hai. Failover karein to us ke baad ki writes ja sakti hain.
Failover
Failover

**Unplanned failover** is for a real outage: the secondary becomes primary, recent data may be lost, and the account becomes **LRS** until you turn geo-redundancy on again. **Planned failover** is for drills: both regions must be healthy, replication finishes first, no data loss is expected and geo-redundancy is kept.

**Unplanned failover** asal outage ke liye: secondary primary banta hai, taza data ja sakta hai, aur account dobara geo on karne tak **LRS** ho jata hai. **Planned failover** drill ke liye: dono regions theek hon, pehle replication mukammal hoti hai, data ka nuqsan mutawaqqe nahi aur geo-redundancy rehti hai.
Limits worth knowing
Yaad rakhne wali hadein

items: Premium accounts: LRS or ZRS only.
Premium accounts: sirf LRS ya ZRS.
Azure Files: no RA options.
Azure Files: RA options nahi.
Archive tier: not on ZRS, GZRS or RA-GZRS.
Archive tier: ZRS, GZRS ya RA-GZRS par nahi.
Durability: LRS 11 nines, ZRS 12 nines, geo options 16 nines.
Durability: LRS 11 nines, ZRS 12 nines, geo options 16 nines.

t: Storage account → Data management → Redundancy · Configuration
Storage account → Data management → Redundancy · Configuration
Redundancy is **not a backup**. If you delete or overwrite a blob, the deletion is copied too. Use soft delete, versioning or Azure Backup for that.
Redundancy **backup nahi**. Blob delete ya overwrite karein to delete bhi copy ho jata hai. Us ke liye soft delete, versioning ya Azure Backup.
An app needs archive *and* reading from a second region. Which redundancy?
App ko archive *aur* doosre region se parhna chahiye. Kaun si redundancy?
a: RA-GRS. The zone-redundant options don't support archive.
RA-GRS. Zone-redundant options archive support nahi karte.

t: After an unplanned failover, what is the account's redundancy?
Unplanned failover ke baad account ki redundancy?
a: LRS, in the new primary region.
LRS, naye primary region mein.

t: Can a standard account become premium later?
Kya standard account baad mein premium ban sakta hai?
a: No. Create a new account and copy the data.
Nahi. Naya account bana kar data copy karein.

t: There are three ways to prove that you may use storage data: the **account key**, a **shared access signature (SAS)** or your **Entra identity**. Security goes up and risk goes down in that order.
Storage data use karne ke teen tareeqe hain: **account key**, **shared access signature (SAS)** ya aap ki **Entra identity**. Isi tarteeb mein hifazat barhti aur khatra ghat-ta hai.
Account keys
Account keys

Each account has **two** keys, and each opens everything. Why two? So you can rotate without downtime: move the apps to key 2, regenerate key 1, move them back, regenerate key 2. Store keys in Key Vault, never in code. A **key expiration policy** reminds you by flagging old keys; it doesn't rotate them. You can forbid keys completely with **Allow storage account key access = Disabled**.

Har account ki **do** keys hain, aur har ek sab kuch kholti hai. Do kyun? Taa ke baghair downtime rotate ho: apps ko key 2 par layen, key 1 dobara banayen, wapas layen, key 2 banayen. Keys Key Vault mein rakhein, code mein kabhi nahi. **Key expiration policy** purani keys flag kar ke yaad dilati hai; khud rotate nahi karti. **Allow storage account key access = Disabled** se keys bilkul band ho jati hain.
SAS: a visitor's pass
SAS: mehmaan ka pass

A SAS is a web address with a signature that says *what, how, until when* and optionally *from which IP*. Whoever has the address has the access, so make it small and short. Read its parts: `sp` permissions, `st`/`se` start and expiry, `sip` IP range, `spr` protocol, `sig` signature.

SAS dastakhat wala web address hai jo kehta hai *kya, kaise, kab tak* aur chahein to *kis IP se*. Jis ke paas address hai us ke paas access hai, is liye chota aur thore waqt ka banayen. Us ke hisse: `sp` permissions, `st`/`se` shuru aur expiry, `sip` IP range, `spr` protocol, `sig` dastakhat.

items: **User delegation SAS**: signed with Entra credentials, no account key involved. The safest; at most 7 days.
**User delegation SAS**: Entra credentials se signed, account key nahi. Sab se mehfooz; zyada se zyada 7 din.
**Service SAS**: signed with the account key, for one service (for example one container).
**Service SAS**: account key se signed, ek service ke liye (maslan ek container).
**Account SAS**: signed with the account key, for several services and account-level operations.
**Account SAS**: account key se signed, kai services aur account-level operations ke liye.

t: Taking a SAS back
SAS wapas lena

An ad-hoc SAS can't be revoked on its own. You'd have to regenerate the key that signed it, which kills *every* SAS from that key. The fix is to plan ahead with a **stored access policy** on the container, share, queue or table (up to five each). The SAS refers to the policy, so when you change or delete the policy, every SAS tied to it changes or dies within about 30 seconds. Policies work with service SAS only. One odd detail: if you delete policy 'p1' and later make a new 'p1', old SAS tokens that refer to the name work again.

Ad-hoc SAS akela revoke nahi hota. Us ko sign karne wali key dobara banani paregi, jis se us key ka *har* SAS khatam. Hal yeh hai ke pehle se container, share, queue ya table par **stored access policy** banayen (har ek par paanch tak). SAS policy ka hawala deta hai, is liye policy badlein ya delete karein to us ke tamam SAS taqreeban 30 second mein badal ya khatam ho jate hain. Policies sirf service SAS ke sath. Ajeeb baat: policy 'p1' delete kar ke baad mein nayi 'p1' banayen to purane SAS phir chalne lagte hain.
Entra ID
Entra ID

The recommended way for apps and people: assign a data role (**Storage Blob Data Reader / Contributor / Owner**, or the queue and table ones) and sign in. Azure-hosted apps use a managed identity. Nothing to leak, nothing to rotate, and every access carries a name.

Apps aur logon ke liye recommended: data role dein (**Storage Blob Data Reader / Contributor / Owner**, ya queue aur table wale) aur sign in karein. Azure ki apps managed identity use karti hain. Na kuch leak hone ko, na rotate karne ko, aur har access par naam.
Encryption
Encryption

All data is **always encrypted at rest**; you can't turn that off. By default Microsoft manages the keys. With **customer-managed keys** the key is in your Key Vault (soft delete and purge protection on), and the account reads it with a managed identity. Give the key URI **without a version** and the account follows key rotation by itself. **Encryption scopes** give different containers different keys. **Secure transfer required** rejects plain HTTP: that's encryption on the way, not at rest.

Tamam data **hamesha encrypted** rakha jata hai; band nahi hota. Default mein keys Microsoft sambhalta hai. **Customer-managed keys** mein key aap ki Key Vault mein hoti hai (soft delete aur purge protection on), aur account managed identity se parhta hai. Key URI **version ke baghair** dein to account rotation ko khud follow karta hai. **Encryption scopes** alag containers ko alag keys dete hain. **Secure transfer required** saada HTTP rokta hai: yeh raaste ki encryption hai, rakhne ki nahi.
A partner needs to download one report for 24 hours. Best: a user delegation SAS on that one blob, read only, HTTPS only, 24 hours. Worst: sending them the account key.
Partner ko ek report 24 ghante download karni hai. Behtareen: us ek blob ka user delegation SAS, sirf read, sirf HTTPS, 24 ghante. Badtareen: account key bhejna.
Storage account → Access keys · Shared access signature · Configuration · Encryption · Container → Access policy
Storage account → Access keys · Shared access signature · Configuration · Encryption · Container → Access policy
A valid SAS or key doesn't open the **firewall**. Both checks must pass.
Valid SAS ya key **firewall** nahi kholti. Dono check pass hon.
A SAS valid for a year leaked, and it has no stored access policy. What do you do?
Saal bhar ka SAS leak ho gaya, stored access policy nahi. Kya karenge?
a: Regenerate the account key that signed it, after moving other users to the second key.
Jis key se signed hai woh dobara banayen, pehle baqi sab ko doosri key par la kar.

t: Can a user delegation SAS use a stored access policy?
Kya user delegation SAS stored access policy use kar sakta hai?
a: No, only a service SAS can.
Nahi, sirf service SAS.

t: Contributor opens a container, shared key access is disabled. Result?
Contributor container kholta hai, shared key access band hai. Nateeja?
a: Denied: no key, and no blob data role.
Deny: key nahi, aur blob data role nahi.

t: Proving who you are isn't enough: the request must also come from an allowed **network**. A new storage account usually accepts connections from all networks. You narrow that with the storage **firewall**, with **private endpoints**, or around several services with a **network security perimeter**.

Pehchan kaafi nahi: request allowed **network** se bhi aani chahiye. Naya storage account aam tor par tamam networks se connection leta hai. Isay storage **firewall**, **private endpoints**, ya kai services ke gird **network security perimeter** se mehdood karte hain.
The firewall
Firewall
Choose *Enabled from selected networks*. Then everything is denied except what you list:
*Enabled from selected networks* chunein. Phir list ke siwa sab deny:

items: **Virtual network rules**: a subnet. The subnet must have the **Microsoft.Storage service endpoint**, or the rule doesn't help. Forgetting the endpoint is the classic exam mistake.
**Virtual network rules**: ek subnet. Subnet par **Microsoft.Storage service endpoint** ho, warna rule bekaar. Endpoint bhoolna exam ki mashhoor ghalti hai.
**IP rules**: public IP addresses or ranges, for example your office. Private ranges such as 10.0.0.0/8 aren't accepted, because storage never sees them.
**IP rules**: public IP addresses ya ranges, maslan aap ka office. 10.0.0.0/8 jaisi private ranges nahi leta, kyunke storage unhein dekhta hi nahi.
**Exceptions**: *Allow trusted Microsoft services* lets Azure Backup, Azure Monitor and similar services in.
**Exceptions**: *Allow trusted Microsoft services* se Azure Backup, Azure Monitor waghera andar aate hain.

t: After you switch on the firewall, backups fail and you can't browse blobs from home, though VMs work. Backups: tick the trusted services exception. Home: add your public IP. The portal runs in *your* browser, so the request comes from your home address.

Firewall on karne ke baad backups fail aur ghar se blobs nahi khulte, VMs chalti hain. Backups: trusted services exception tick karein. Ghar: apna public IP dalein. Portal *aap ke* browser mein chalta hai, is liye request ghar ke address se aati hai.
Service endpoint or private endpoint
Service endpoint ya private endpoint

With a **service endpoint**, traffic from the subnet takes the Azure backbone and carries the subnet's identity, but the storage account keeps its public address. It's free, and it doesn't work from on-premises. With a **private endpoint**, the storage account gets a *private IP in your VNet*. It works over VPN and ExpressRoute, and you can close the public side completely. It costs money per hour and needs a **private DNS zone** such as `privatelink.blob.core.windows.net`, or names still resolve to the public address. Each sub-service (blob, file, queue, table, web, dfs) needs its own private endpoint.

**Service endpoint** mein subnet ka traffic Azure backbone se subnet ki pehchan ke sath jata hai, lekin storage ka public address rehta hai. Free hai, on-premises se nahi chalta. **Private endpoint** mein storage account ko *aap ke VNet mein private IP* milta hai. VPN aur ExpressRoute se chalta hai, aur public taraf bilkul band ho sakti hai. Per hour paisa lagta hai aur `privatelink.blob.core.windows.net` jaisa **private DNS zone** chahiye, warna naam public address par hi jata hai. Har sub-service (blob, file, queue, table, web, dfs) ka apna private endpoint.
Watch one effect: after you enable a service endpoint, the storage firewall sees the VM's *private* address. An IP rule with the VM's public address stops matching. Use the subnet rule instead.
Ek asar yaad rakhein: service endpoint on hone ke baad storage firewall ko VM ka *private* address dikhta hai. VM ke public address wala IP rule match nahi karta. Us ki jagah subnet rule.
Network security perimeter
Network security perimeter

A perimeter is a fence around several PaaS resources (storage accounts, key vaults and more). Members may talk to each other; public traffic in or out needs an access rule. *Transition mode* (the default) is for learning what traffic exists, *Enforced mode* blocks what no rule allows. Private endpoint traffic doesn't need a rule. It's newer than the firewall and good to recognize.

Perimeter kai PaaS resources (storage accounts, key vaults waghera) ke gird baarh hai. Members aapas mein baat kar sakte hain; andar ya bahar ke public traffic ko access rule chahiye. *Transition mode* (default) traffic samajhne ke liye, *Enforced mode* baghair rule ka traffic rokta hai. Private endpoint ke traffic ko rule nahi chahiye. Firewall se naya hai, pehchanna kaafi hai.
Anonymous access
Anonymous access

The account setting *Allow blob anonymous access* is the master switch. If it's on, each container is Private, **Blob** (anyone can read a blob whose address they know) or **Container** (anyone can also list). Leave it off unless you host public files.

Account ki setting *Allow blob anonymous access* master switch hai. On ho to har container Private, **Blob** (address maloom ho to koi bhi parhe) ya **Container** (list bhi kare). Public files na hon to band rakhein.
Storage account → Security + networking → Networking
Storage account → Security + networking → Networking
*On-premises must reach storage privately* always means private endpoint. A service endpoint can't do it.
*On-premises se private tareeqe se storage* ka matlab hamesha private endpoint. Service endpoint nahi kar sakta.
Subnet rule added, VMs still blocked. What is missing?
Subnet rule lagaya, VMs phir bhi block. Kya nahi?
a: The Microsoft.Storage service endpoint on that subnet.
Us subnet par Microsoft.Storage service endpoint.

t: Private endpoint exists, but the name resolves to a public IP. Why?
Private endpoint hai, lekin naam public IP par jata hai. Kyun?
a: The privatelink DNS zone isn't linked to the VM's VNet (or its custom DNS server doesn't forward).
privatelink DNS zone VM ke VNet se linked nahi (ya custom DNS server forward nahi karta).

t: Can you allow 192.168.1.0/24 in the IP rules?
Kya IP rules mein 192.168.1.0/24 allow kar sakte hain?
a: No, only public addresses.
Nahi, sirf public addresses.

t: **Blob storage** keeps files as objects in **containers**. There are three kinds: **block blobs** (documents, images, backups: almost everything), **append blobs** (logs, only added to) and **page blobs** (random read and write, disks). Folders are only part of the name, unless the account has a *hierarchical namespace* (Data Lake), which gives real folders and permissions.

**Blob storage** files ko **containers** mein objects ki tarah rakhta hai. Teen qismein: **block blobs** (documents, tasveerein, backups: taqreeban sab), **append blobs** (logs, sirf barhte hain) aur **page blobs** (random read write, disks). Folder sirf naam ka hissa hain, jab tak account par *hierarchical namespace* (Data Lake) na ho, jo asli folders aur permissions deta hai.
Access tiers
Access tiers

You choose between paying for *storing* and paying for *reading*. **Hot** stores expensively and reads cheaply. **Cool** (minimum 30 days) and **Cold** (90 days) store cheaper and read dearer, but are still instant. **Archive** (180 days) is the cheapest shelf in the basement: the blob is **offline** and must be *rehydrated* first, up to 15 hours at standard priority, often under an hour at high priority for small objects. Delete or move a blob before its minimum days and you pay for the rest.

Aap *rakhne* aur *parhne* ke kharche mein chunte hain. **Hot** rakhna mehnga, parhna sasta. **Cool** (kam se kam 30 din) aur **Cold** (90 din) rakhna sasta, parhna mehnga, lekin foran. **Archive** (180 din) tehkhane ki sab se sasti shelf: blob **offline** hai aur pehle *rehydrate* karna parta hai, standard priority mein 15 ghante tak, high priority mein chhote objects aksar ek ghante se kam. Minimum dinon se pehle delete ya move karein to baqi dinon ka paisa.

The account has a default tier (hot, cool, cold or smart); archive is set on single blobs. **Smart tier** (standard GPv2 with zone redundancy) moves blobs between hot, cool and cold by itself: cool after 30 days without access, cold after 90, back to hot when read. It never archives.

Account ki default tier hoti hai (hot, cool, cold ya smart); archive akele blob par. **Smart tier** (zone redundancy wala standard GPv2) khud hot, cool aur cold mein move karta hai: 30 din access na ho to cool, 90 par cold, parhne par wapas hot. Archive kabhi nahi.
Lifecycle management
Lifecycle management

A lifecycle policy is a set of rules: *if a blob hasn't been modified (or read, or created) for X days, move it to cool, cold or archive, or delete it.* Rules run about once a day, so a new rule can take a day or two to show an effect. Rules on 'last read' need **access time tracking**. Append blobs can only be deleted by rules, not tiered.

Lifecycle policy rules ka set hai: *blob X din se modify (ya read, ya create) na hua ho to cool, cold ya archive mein le jao, ya delete.* Rules taqreeban din mein ek dafa chalte hain, is liye naye rule ka asar ek do din mein dikhta hai. 'Last read' rules ko **access time tracking** chahiye. Append blobs rules se sirf delete hote hain, tier nahi.
Protecting data from mistakes
Ghaltiyon se data bachana

items: **Soft delete** (blobs and containers): deleted things wait 1 to 365 days and can be undeleted.
**Soft delete** (blobs aur containers): delete hui cheez 1 se 365 din intezar karti hai aur wapas aa sakti hai.
**Versioning**: every overwrite or delete keeps the old version automatically. Restore by making an old version current. Each version is stored and billed.
**Versioning**: har overwrite ya delete par purana version khud rehta hai. Purana version current bana kar wapas layen. Har version ka paisa lagta hai.
**Snapshot**: a read-only copy you take by hand.
**Snapshot**: haath se li gayi read-only copy.
**Point-in-time restore**: bring block blobs in a range back to an earlier moment. Needs versioning, change feed and soft delete.
**Point-in-time restore**: block blobs ko pehle ke waqt par le jana. Versioning, change feed aur soft delete chahiye.
**Immutable storage (WORM)**: nobody can change or delete, not even an admin. *Time-based retention* for a period, *legal hold* until removed. A **locked** retention policy can only be extended.
**Immutable storage (WORM)**: koi badal ya delete nahi kar sakta, admin bhi nahi. *Time-based retention* muqarrar arsa, *legal hold* hatane tak. **Locked** policy sirf barhayi ja sakti hai.

t: Object replication
Object replication

Copies block blobs **asynchronously** to another account, even in another region or subscription. Requirements: **versioning on both** sides and **change feed on the source**. The destination container becomes read-only for clients. Archived blobs aren't replicated. Use it to bring data near readers, not as a replacement for GRS.

Block blobs ko **asynchronously** doosre account mein copy karta hai, doosre region ya subscription mein bhi. Shartein: **dono taraf versioning** aur **source par change feed**. Destination container clients ke liye read-only ho jata hai. Archive blobs replicate nahi hote. Data parhne walon ke qareeb lane ke liye, GRS ki jagah nahi.

A camera uploads videos: watched often for two weeks, rarely for a year, then never needed. Upload to hot; lifecycle: cool after 14 days, cold after 90, delete after 365. If they also must not be changed by law, add a time-based retention policy to the container.

Camera videos upload karta hai: do hafte aksar dekhi jati hain, saal bhar kabhi kabhi, phir kabhi nahi. Hot mein upload; lifecycle: 14 din baad cool, 90 baad cold, 365 baad delete. Qanoonan badalni na hon to container par time-based retention.
Storage account → Data protection · Lifecycle management · Object replication · Container → Access policy (immutability)
Storage account → Data protection · Lifecycle management · Object replication · Container → Access policy (immutability)
A lock on the storage account doesn't protect the blobs inside. For data use soft delete, versioning or immutability.
Storage account par lock andar ke blobs ko nahi bachata. Data ke liye soft delete, versioning ya immutability.
A blob in archive is needed in one hour. What can you do?
Archive ka blob ek ghante mein chahiye. Kya kar sakte hain?
a: Rehydrate with high priority (it may finish within an hour for small objects), or keep such data in cold instead.
High priority se rehydrate (chhote objects aksar ghante mein), ya aisa data cold mein rakhein.

t: Someone overwrote a file. Versioning is on. How do you get it back?
Kisi ne file overwrite kar di. Versioning on hai. Wapas kaise?
a: Make the previous version the current version.
Pichla version current version banayen.

t: Which two settings does object replication need?
Object replication ko kaun si do settings chahiye?
a: Versioning on both accounts and change feed on the source.
Dono accounts par versioning aur source par change feed.

t: **Azure Files** is a file server without the server: shares that Windows, Linux and macOS can mount. **SMB** shares use TCP port **445**. Many home providers block 445, which is why mounting works in the office and fails at home (*System error 53*). The answers are a VPN or ExpressRoute, or Azure File Sync. **NFS** shares are for Linux, in premium accounts.

**Azure Files** server ke baghair file server hai: shares jo Windows, Linux aur macOS mount karte hain. **SMB** shares TCP port **445** use karte hain. Ghar ke kai providers 445 block karte hain, is liye office mein mount hota hai aur ghar mein fail (*System error 53*). Hal: VPN ya ExpressRoute, ya Azure File Sync. **NFS** shares Linux ke liye, premium accounts mein.
Who may open the share
Share kaun khol sakta hai
With the account key anybody is administrator. Better is **identity-based access**. A storage account uses exactly **one** identity source:
Account key se har koi administrator hai. Behtar **identity-based access** hai. Storage account theek **ek** identity source use karta hai:

items: **AD DS** (your own domain): users must be hybrid, that is synced to Entra ID, and the storage account must be joined to the domain.
**AD DS** (aap ka apna domain): users hybrid hon, yani Entra ID se synced, aur storage account domain se joined ho.
**Microsoft Entra Domain Services**: the managed domain in Azure.
**Microsoft Entra Domain Services**: Azure ka managed domain.
**Microsoft Entra Kerberos**: for hybrid users, and in the public cloud also for cloud-only users, from suitable Entra-joined clients. MFA must be excluded for the storage account's app.
**Microsoft Entra Kerberos**: hybrid users ke liye, aur public cloud mein cloud-only users ke liye bhi, munasib Entra-joined clients se. Storage account ki app ke liye MFA exclude karni hoti hai.

t: Then **two locks** must both open. The **share-level** permission is an Azure role: *Storage File Data SMB Share Reader*, *Contributor* (read, write, delete) or *Elevated Contributor* (also change NTFS permissions). The **directory and file level** is normal NTFS permissions. The stricter of the two wins. Instead of many role assignments you can set a *default share-level permission* for all authenticated identities and control the rest with NTFS.

Phir **do taale** dono khulne chahiye. **Share-level** permission Azure role hai: *Storage File Data SMB Share Reader*, *Contributor* (read, write, delete) ya *Elevated Contributor* (NTFS permissions bhi badalna). **Directory aur file level** aam NTFS permissions hain. Dono mein se sakht jeetta hai. Bohat se role assignments ki jagah tamam authenticated identities ke liye *default share-level permission* rakh kar baqi NTFS se control kar sakte hain.
Snapshots, soft delete, backup
Snapshots, soft delete, backup

A **share snapshot** is a read-only picture of the whole share; only changes take space. People restore their own files through *Previous Versions* in Windows. Up to 200 snapshots per share. **Soft delete** protects the share itself: a deleted share waits 1 to 365 days (7 by default). It does *not* bring back a single file. **Azure Backup** schedules snapshots for you, and with **vaulted backup** also copies the data to a vault, which survives even if the storage account is deleted.

**Share snapshot** poore share ki read-only tasveer hai; sirf tabdeeliyan jagah leti hain. Log Windows ke *Previous Versions* se apni files wapas late hain. Har share ke 200 snapshots tak. **Soft delete** khud share ko bachata hai: delete hua share 1 se 365 din (default 7) rehta hai. Ek file wapas *nahi* lata. **Azure Backup** snapshots schedule karta hai, aur **vaulted backup** data vault mein bhi copy karta hai, jo storage account delete hone par bhi bachta hai.
Azure File Sync
Azure File Sync

File Sync joins your Windows file servers with an Azure share. You create a *Storage Sync Service*, install the agent on the server and register it, then build a **sync group**: exactly **one cloud endpoint** (the Azure share) and any number of **server endpoints** (folders on servers). **Cloud tiering** keeps hot files on the server and replaces cold ones with pointers that download when opened. Users notice only that the disk no longer fills up.

File Sync aap ke Windows file servers ko Azure share se jorta hai. *Storage Sync Service* banayen, server par agent install kar ke register karein, phir **sync group**: theek **ek cloud endpoint** (Azure share) aur jitne chahein **server endpoints** (servers ke folders). **Cloud tiering** garam files server par rakhta hai aur thandi ki jagah pointers, jo kholne par download hote hain. Users ko sirf yeh pata chalta hai ke disk ab nahi bharti.

Three branches each need fast access to the same 5 TB, and the branch servers have small disks: one Azure share, File Sync on each branch server, cloud tiering on. One sync group, one cloud endpoint, three server endpoints.

Teen branches ko ek hi 5 TB tak tez access chahiye, aur servers ki disks choti hain: ek Azure share, har branch server par File Sync, cloud tiering on. Ek sync group, ek cloud endpoint, teen server endpoints.
Billing models in one line
Billing ek line mein

*Pay-as-you-go* (HDD) bills used space and transactions, with tiers Transaction optimized, Hot and Cool. *Provisioned v2*, recommended for new shares, lets you set storage, IOPS and throughput separately; a value can be lowered only 24 hours after its last increase.

*Pay-as-you-go* (HDD) istemal hui jagah aur transactions ka bill, tiers Transaction optimized, Hot aur Cool. *Provisioned v2*, naye shares ke liye recommended, storage, IOPS aur throughput alag set karne deta hai; value aakhri izafe ke 24 ghante baad hi kam hoti hai.
Storage account → File shares → share → Snapshots / Backup · File shares → Identity-based access / Soft delete
Storage account → File shares → share → Snapshots / Backup · File shares → Identity-based access / Soft delete
*Contributor* on the storage account gives **no** identity-based access to files. You need a *Storage File Data SMB Share* role plus NTFS.
Storage account ka *Contributor* files ka identity-based access **nahi** deta. *Storage File Data SMB Share* role aur NTFS chahiye.
A user deleted one file and only soft delete is on. Can you get it back?
User ne ek file delete ki aur sirf soft delete on hai. Wapas aayegi?
a: Not with soft delete. You need a snapshot or a backup.
Soft delete se nahi. Snapshot ya backup chahiye.

t: How many cloud endpoints can a sync group have?
Sync group mein kitne cloud endpoints?
a: One.
Ek.

t: Admins must change NTFS permissions. Which share-level role?
Admins NTFS permissions badlein. Kaun sa share-level role?
a: Storage File Data SMB Share Elevated Contributor.
Storage File Data SMB Share Elevated Contributor.

t: Three questions decide the tool: *How much data? How fast is the network? Once or again and again?*
Teen sawal tool tay karte hain: *Kitna data? Network kitna tez? Ek dafa ya baar baar?*
AzCopy
AzCopy

**AzCopy** is a command-line tool for copying to, from and between storage accounts. Between two accounts it copies **server to server**: the data doesn't pass through your computer. Sign in with `azcopy login` (Entra ID, then you need a role such as *Storage Blob Data Contributor*) or put a SAS at the end of the address.

**AzCopy** storage accounts mein, se aur ke darmiyan copy karne ka command-line tool hai. Do accounts ke darmiyan **server to server** copy karta hai: data aap ke computer se nahi guzarta. `azcopy login` (Entra ID, phir *Storage Blob Data Contributor* jaisa role) se sign in karein ya address ke aakhir mein SAS lagayen.

items: `azcopy copy` copies everything you name. Add `--recursive` for folders.
`azcopy copy` jo likhein sab copy. Folders ke liye `--recursive`.
`azcopy sync` copies only what changed, comparing source and destination. `--delete-destination=true` also removes files at the destination that no longer exist at the source.
`azcopy sync` sirf tabdeeliyan, source aur destination ka muqabla kar ke. `--delete-destination=true` destination ki woh files bhi hatata hai jo source mein nahi rahin.
`azcopy make` creates a container or share, `azcopy remove` deletes, `azcopy jobs resume` continues an interrupted transfer.
`azcopy make` container ya share banata hai, `azcopy remove` delete, `azcopy jobs resume` ruka hua transfer jari karta hai.

t: Nightly upload of a folder where little changes: `azcopy sync 'C:\data' 'https://acct.blob.core.windows.net/c?SAS'`. With `copy` you'd upload everything every night.
Rozana folder upload jis mein kam badalta hai: `azcopy sync 'C:\data' 'https://acct.blob.core.windows.net/c?SAS'`. `copy` se har raat sab upload hota.
Storage Explorer
Storage Explorer

**Azure Storage Explorer** is a free desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux. It's the friendly way to browse blobs, files, queues and tables, upload by drag and drop, and create SAS tokens. Connect by signing in, or with an account name and key, a SAS, or a connection string. Behind the scenes it uses AzCopy.

**Azure Storage Explorer** Windows, macOS aur Linux ki free desktop app hai. Blobs, files, queues aur tables dekhne, drag and drop upload karne aur SAS banane ka aasan tareeqa. Sign in se, ya account name aur key, SAS, ya connection string se connect. Andar se AzCopy use karti hai.
When the network is too slow
Network bohat slow ho

Do the sum. 60 TB over a 100 Mbit/s line takes about two months. For that, ship disks: **Azure Data Box** (Microsoft sends a device, you fill it and send it back) or **Import/Export** (you send your own drives). The exam hint is *large amount of data* plus *limited bandwidth*.

Hisab karein. 60 TB, 100 Mbit/s par taqreeban do mahine. Is ke liye disks bhejein: **Azure Data Box** (Microsoft device bhejta hai, aap bhar kar wapas) ya **Import/Export** (aap apni drives bhejte hain). Exam ka ishara: *bohat data* aur *kam bandwidth*.
Moving an account to another region
Account doosre region mein

There's no 'change region' button. Export a template if you want the same settings, create a new account in the target region, copy the data (AzCopy), and switch the apps. Moving to another *resource group or subscription* is a normal move and keeps the region.

'Region badlo' button nahi. Same settings chahiye to template export karein, target region mein naya account banayen, data copy (AzCopy), aur apps badlein. Doosre *resource group ya subscription* mein move aam hai aur region wahi rehta hai.

Doosre naam

items: **SFTP for Blob storage**: partners upload with SFTP. Needs the hierarchical namespace and local users.
**SFTP for Blob storage**: partners SFTP se upload. Hierarchical namespace aur local users chahiye.
**Static website**: serves HTML from the `$web` container.
**Static website**: `$web` container se HTML deta hai.
**Azure Storage Mover / Migrate**: services for moving file shares and servers.
**Azure Storage Mover / Migrate**: file shares aur servers le jane ki services.

t: Watching storage
Storage ko dekhna

**Storage insights** in Azure Monitor shows capacity, latency and availability for all accounts with no setup. Throttling appears in the *Transactions* metric, filtered by **ResponseType** (for example ServerBusyError). To see *who read or deleted a blob*, create a **diagnostic setting** on the blob service with the StorageRead, StorageWrite and StorageDelete logs.

Azure Monitor ki **Storage insights** baghair setup tamam accounts ki capacity, latency aur availability dikhati hai. Throttling *Transactions* metric mein **ResponseType** se filter (maslan ServerBusyError) par dikhti hai. *Blob kis ne parha ya delete kiya* ke liye blob service par StorageRead, StorageWrite aur StorageDelete logs ki **diagnostic setting** banayen.
Storage account → Storage browser · Resource group → Move · Monitor → Storage accounts (insights) · Storage account → Diagnostic settings → blob
Storage account → Storage browser · Resource group → Move · Monitor → Storage accounts (insights) · Storage account → Diagnostic settings → blob
AzCopy with `azcopy login` fails with 403 although you're Owner of the account? Owner has no blob data actions. Add a Storage Blob Data role.
`azcopy login` ke sath 403 aata hai halanke aap account ke Owner hain? Owner mein blob data actions nahi. Storage Blob Data role lagayen.
Copy 10 TB between two storage accounts. Does it pass through your laptop?
Do storage accounts mein 10 TB copy. Kya aap ke laptop se guzrega?
a: No, AzCopy copies server to server.
Nahi, AzCopy server to server copy karta hai.

t: copy or sync: only changed files, and removed files should disappear too.
copy ya sync: sirf badli files, aur hatayi gayi files bhi hat jayen.
a: azcopy sync with --delete-destination=true.
azcopy sync, --delete-destination=true ke sath.

t: How do you connect Storage Explorer for a partner who may see one container?
Partner ko ek container dikhana hai. Storage Explorer kaise connect ho?
a: Give them a SAS URL for that container.
Us container ka SAS URL dein.
